title: Release gate: functions above CCN 15
cluster_summary: Each repo crossed the automated-tests-§3 tag gate (zero sighted functions above CCN 15, blindFiles 0) through its own recent commits, so the fix is per-repo and no upstream change applies. AuraMaster has 1 function over (18), BankLedger has 1 (16, reported twice as BL-A-02 and BL-R-01, now merged into one item), and LootHistory has 26-27 introduced since f31727b (2026-10-01), several by the v13 migration. These are real regressions, not old debt that sighting exposed: convertHolderMoves, accumulateLedger and planHolder did not exist at f31727b. PrettyChat's listSettings sits at exactly 15, which does not breach the gate. Recommendation: fix AM and BL with named-helper extractions. Phase LH by file, writing a characterization test first and taking the v13 migration last. Track any guard-ladder function that can only get under 15 through metric-driven splitting (#52) as a deviation, so the tag gate stays meaningful.

verdicts.assessment: The sighted run measures logCandidates (modules/Anchors_Snap.lua:892) at CCN 18. It came in with cb766da and blocks the next tag under automated-tests-§3. It runs only on the debug path, so players are not affected, but the fix is small and existing DD-21 cases already pin the output.
verdicts.remediation: Extract a named helper, targetText(dragged, t), and hoist the outcome and target suffixes into locals. Log output must stay byte-identical, with the DD-21 cases green. Re-measure through the sighted runner (target: logCandidates <=12, blindFiles 0). Do not use a Part2 split or an if-ladder (#52). If no honest helper gets it to 15 or below, record a tracked deviation.

verdicts.assessment: This duplicates BL-R-01: the same function (LT.GroupEntries, CCN 16) with the same cause ('or groupOrder' at :339 from 5a78432). It is a real tag-gate blocker. Close it together with BL-R-01 in one commit and do not plan it as separate work.
verdicts.remediation: Merged into BL-R-01. Carry both ids on the single commit (BL-R-01 + BL-A-02).

verdicts.assessment: This is the canonical item for LT.GroupEntries at sighted CCN 16, the only BankLedger function over the gate. It is defaulting density rather than tangled logic. The fix is cheap and keeps the next tag unblocked.
verdicts.remediation: Write a characterization case first (typesub grouping, descending order). Then hoist the sort-key or comparator logic to module scope. Choose ONE shape: either a groupSortKey(sortFn, e, order, label) helper or groupAscending/groupDescending comparators selected by self.groupAsc, so there is no per-call closure. Keep precedence identical, re-measure sighted (blindFiles 0), and regenerate the inventory and badge.

verdicts.assessment: Real regressions: the sighted run at f31727b measured 0, and convertHolderMoves, accumulateLedger and planHolder did not exist there (the v13 work, 3449101 and later, added them). The necessity lens's claim that this is only old debt that sighting exposed is wrong. The location list also leaves out Reconciler planHolder@192 (CCN 19), so the cited set has 27 locations against a count of 26. Re-measure before planning. Nothing ships broken and no tag is planned, but the debt is new and growing.
verdicts.remediation: Re-measure through the sighted runner and fix the exact list (add Reconciler:192). Work file by file, one commit per file, writing a characterization test before each change. Start with the real branching (CCN >=20: convertHolderMoves, StandUp, Database.Stats, onEvent, accumulateLedger, Holdings.Search) and split it into named helpers. Use file-scope ordered lists for guard ladders. Touch the Database v13 migration only after a characterization case covers it. Do not use in-function dispatch tables or metric-only splits (#52). Any function left that cannot honestly reach 15 or below becomes a tracked deviation with an ID and owner (#53). Move the inventory and badge with the count.

verdicts.assessment: listSettings measures exactly CCN 15. The gate fires only above 15, and nothing else in PrettyChat breaches it. Refactoring now would just move a number (#52). The reviewer's own verdict was no action.
